extracted.intended_audience: patent researchers, librarians, historians, archivists, and USPTO catalogers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for compiling or interpreting an alphabetical index of issued patents (1878 US Patent Office style), specifying the metadata fields and organization used for each entry (title, patentee, patent number, issue date, monthly volume, Official Gazette reference). Useful for cataloguing, searching, or digitizing historical patent records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical list of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are organized alphabetically by the invention or discovery title; the page is an 'Alphabetical list of inventions—Continued.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group and order entries by the invention title (headword). Example headwords shown: 'Bed-bottom', 'Bee-hive', 'Beer, Apparatus for preserving', etc. Maintain sequence across pages for continuity when the list continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention or discovery (title/headword)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first column records the invention or discovery name (title or headword) as the primary searchable label for the entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the inventor-provided short title or conventional descriptive phrase, including hyphenation and modifiers (e.g., 'Bed-bottom, Spring', 'Bee-hive', 'Boiler-furnace grate, Steam'). Entries may include variants and subtypes separated by commas or dashes; preserve original punctuation and phrasing as printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name of patentee
rubrics_metrics.description: The second column lists the patentee(s) associated with the patent (inventor(s) or assignees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record full names or initials as presented, including multiple names separated with commas and 'and' (e.g., 'E. J. Johnson and M. E. Mills', 'T. W. B. Murray and C. J. Baker'). Preserve ordering and punctuation exactly as printed for provenance and searchability.

rubrics_metrics.name: No. (patent number)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'No.' column gives the issued U.S. patent number for the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture the numeric patent identifier as printed (often with thousands separator commas in this document, e.g., '206,256', '199,513'). This number is the primary identifier for cross-referencing the full patent specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date (issue date)
rubrics_metrics.description: A column records the official issue date of the patent (month and day, year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcribe the issue date in the form shown on the page (month name possibly abbreviated, day, and year—e.g., 'May 21, 1878', 'Oct. 29, 1878'). Maintain printed punctuation/abbreviations for fidelity to the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly volume
rubrics_metrics.description: A column indicating the monthly volume number in which the patent was reported or indexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the monthly volume as shown (numeric). This links the index entry to the periodical/monthly reporting structure used by the Office; examples on the page include values like '199', '210', etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A column giving the Official Gazette reference associated with the patent entry (page/issue or reference code used in the Office's Gazette).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcribe the Gazette reference exactly as printed to enable locating the patent notice in the Official Gazette. Examples on the page are numeric codes and page references that appear in the rightmost column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references and see-also notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Index includes cross-references directing the reader to related headwords (e.g., 'See "Wash-bench.'', 'Work-bench.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve and include 'See' or 'See "X"' notes so users can follow alternative headings or related entries. Such cross-references are part of the index structure and improve discoverability across variant terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple and compound entry handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The index handles compound inventions and multiple related sub-entries under a headword (e.g., multiple 'Bed-bottom, Spring' variants, many types of 'Boiler' entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When cataloging, keep distinct subtypes as separate index lines (even if similar headwords repeat) and preserve subtype qualifiers (e.g., 'Boiler, Tubular', 'Boiler, Sectional'). This preserves specificity for retrieval and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve printed orthography and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: The index preserves 19th-century spelling, hyphenation, and punctuation conventions as printed in the original USPTO annual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For historical accuracy and faithful digitization, transcribe entries verbatim, including obsolete spellings or varying hyphenation (examples: 'Bee-liivo', 'Bec-hive' variants appear in the text). Note OCR or typographical noise where present.
